messages:
sam_support: Hey team, customers reporting usage graphs in Console are delayed by ~3-4 hours for a subset of tenants. Saw a spike in support tickets starting ~02:00 UTC. Any idea if ETL jobs failed?
violet_oncall: @sam_support seeing alert from metrics-bot: hourly-rollup DAG had 3 failed tasks at 01:56 UTC. I restarted the DAG but backlog still shows. :eyes:
metrics-bot: ALERT: dag_id=hourly_rollups run_id=scheduled__2026-10-14T01:00:00 failed_tasks=3 failed_at=2026-10-14T01:56:12Z
deploy-bot: INFO: connector-kafka-consumer restarted by violet_oncall at 2026-10-14T02:02:09Z (uptime checking)
sam_support: Customer list includes: acme-inc, beta-labs, cafezero. They see embeddings/usage counters stuck. Screenshots attached in ticket: counts stop at 01:00 UTC.
ben_eng: I pulled the rollup task logs for 01:00. Error is intermittent DB timeout writing to hourly_rollups table: "psycopg2.OperationalError: could not serialize access due to concurrent update" repeated.
maria_data: That suggests write contention during the partition compaction. We're doing a heavy backfill on older partitions this morning (backfill-backfill-2026-10-14). Could be saturating writer pool.
ben_eng: Confirmed: backfill job spawned multiple parallel workers; noticed increased connection count to analytics-db from 40 -> 160 at 01:45 UTC. Postgres CPU spiked to 98% and started timing out.
violet_oncall: I scaled write pool down to 20 and queued remaining backfill tasks, but hourly DAG retries are still queued. How long to drain the queue?
maria_data: If we pause the backfill and let hourly_rollups catch up, should clear in ~90 minutes. Alternative is to pause hourly_rollups and run controlled one-off backfills with rate-limit. Prefer un-pausing critical dashboards first.
sam_support: Customers asking ETA. Can we push a priority run for impacted tenants only?
ben_eng: Yes — we can run targeted rollups for the three affected tenants. Steps:
1) Pause global backfill job: `airflow dags pause backfill-backfill-2026-10-14`
2) Run targeted task: `python infra/tools/run_rollup.py --tenant acme-inc,beta-labs,cafezero --hour 01`
3) Monitor `SELECT count(*) FROM hourly_rollups WHERE tenant_id IN (...) AND hour = '2026-10-14 01:00:00'` in analytics-db.
ben_eng: I'll kick off the targeted run now.
metrics-bot: INFO: job started run_id=targeted_rollup_2123456802 by ben_eng
customer_ops: Please include in customer comms: "We're working on restoring delayed metrics; some dashboards will catch up within ~90 minutes. Apologies for the disruption."
violet_oncall: Reminder: set connection_pool=30 for the targeted run and disable parallel shard scanners to avoid repeat contention.
ben_eng: Done. Running with pool=30 and shard_concurrency=1. Log tail:
```
2026-10-14T02:07:03Z | rollup | INFO | starting targeted rollup for tenant acme-inc
2026-10-14T02:07:45Z | db | WARNING | write retry 1 due to serialization failure
2026-10-14T02:08:12Z | rollup | INFO | completed tenant acme-inc in 18s
```
ben_eng: acme-inc done. Starting beta-labs...
sam_support: Customer acme-inc confirmed their dashboard updated for the 01:00 hour. Thanks.
ben_eng: beta-labs and cafezero completed. I see the backlog for hourly_rollups drop from 180 -> 24 tasks.
violet_oncall: I'm keeping backfill paused and will gradually resume at lower concurrency after a maintenance window message.
maria_data: Postmortem action items: limit backfill parallelism by default, add DB connection safety throttle, and add a backpressure signal to the backfill coordinator so it stops if DB latency > 500ms.
sam_support: I'll update affected customers: ETA for remaining catch-up ~60 minutes. Send a banner in Console?
customer_ops: Sending a banner: "Metrics are delayed due to temporary ingest load. We expect full recovery within 1 hour. For urgent concerns contact support"
ben_eng: Will follow up with a brief runbook for oncall: how to detect backfill-induced contention and steps to run targeted rollups.
violet_oncall: Thanks all — marking incident resolved for support routing. If we see resumed DB timeouts after resume, I'll reopen. :white_check_mark:
